source_text: Qui ergo contra hanc sententiam dicit traducem esse peccati, dicat quoque recursum esse peccati ut, si a parentibus ad filios peccata descendunt, ascendant a filiis ad parentes, quoniam divinae legis ostendit auctoritas ita parentum crimina filiis non nocere sicut nec parentibus filiorum.
pass_a_gloss: Whoever therefore against this sentence says there is a vine-layer of sin, let him also say there is a running-back of sin, so that if sins descend from parents to sons they also ascend from sons to parents, since the authority of the divine law shows that parents' crimes do not harm sons just as sons' crimes do not harm parents.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Therefore, anyone who contradicts this pronouncement by saying that sin is transmitted should also say that sin travels back again. If sins descend from parents to children, let them also ascend from children to parents, since the authority of divine law shows that parents’ crimes do not harm their children, just as children’s crimes do not harm their parents (Deuteronomy 24:16).

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
